REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.di ig.gov.ph DIR. REYNALDO M. BUNGUBUNG, CESE Officer-in -Charge DILG-Region XII Sumpay Bldg., Block IV Maranon Village, Barangay Zone III Koronadal City Dear Dir. Bungubung: DILG Legal Opinion No. 22 APR BNAHENG PINOY 9. 14, s. 2014 2014 This has reference to your 1st Indorsement dated 01 April 2014 forwarding to the Central Office pertinent documents requesting guidance as to the legality of appointment of Ms. Violeta T. Tabugo as Women's Sectoral Representative to the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Cotabato City, with the following attachments: 1. 2. Letter dated 24 January 2014 from Dir. Guiano D. Abdilah, DILG-Cotabato City, with the following supporting documents: a. SP Resolution No. 5424 dated 26 November 2013 entitled "A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE HONORABLE CITY MAYOR JAPAL J. GUIANI, JR. TO APPOINT A SECTORAL REPRESEMATIVE FOR WOMEN TO THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF COTABATO CITY, SUBJECT TO EXISTING LAWS, RULES AND REGULATIONS"; b. Executive Order No. 97 dated 09 December 2013 entitled "CONSTITUTING A SCREENING COMMITTEE AND PRESCRIBING THE GUIDELINES AND CRITERIA IN THE SELECTION OF WOMEN'S SECTORAL REPRESENTATIVE TO THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD", c. Photocopy of Ms. Tabugo's Oath of Office. Letter dated 23 January 2014 from Acting City Mayor Hadji Abdullah A. Andang, Sr., informing you of the foregoing. At the outset, it may be well to stress that SP Resolution No. 5424 dated 26 November 2013 was already adopted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Cotabato City. Likewise, Executive Order No. 97 dated 09 December 2013 was already issued by Mayor Guiani. Such being the case, said issuances enjoy the presumption of validity and thus are presumed valid unless later judicially invalidated by a court of justice.

However, for academic discussion coupled with our objective to guide the parties on the course/s of action to take under the circumstances, please be informed that Section 41 (b) and (c) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 provides: "(b) The regular members OT the sangguniang pan/a/awigan, sangguniang panlungsod, and sangguniang bayan shall be elected by district, as may be provided for by law. Sangguniang barangay members shall be elected at large. The presidents of the leagues of Sanggunian members of' component cities and municipalities shall serve as ex-officio members of the sangguniang pan/alawigan concerned. The presidents of the liga ng mga barangay and the pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan elected by their respective chapters, as provided in this Code, shall serve as ex-officio members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, and sangguniang bayan. (c) In addition thereto, there shall be one (1) sectoral representative from the women, one (1) from the workers, and one (1) from any of the following sectors: the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons, or any other sector as may be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (SO) days prior to the holding of the next local elections, as may be provided for by law. The COMELEC shall promulgate the rules and regulations to effectively provide for the election of such sectoral representatives. With respect to cities, Section 457 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides that: "SEC. 457. Composition.- (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, the legislative body of the city, shall be composed of the city vice mayor as presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the city chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, the president of the panlungsod na pedersayon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, and the sectoral representatives, as members. (b) In addition thereto, there shall be three (3) sectoral representatives: one (1) from the women; and, as shall be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the local elections, one (1) from the agricultural or industrial workers; and one (1) from the other sectors, including the urban poor, indigenous cultural minorities, or disabled persons. (c) The regular members of the sangguniangpanlungsod and the ctoralr r naiv hall elect inth mannr s ma for by law. " (underlining ours) It is clear that under Section 41 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sanggunian, in addition to the regular and ex-officio members, shall be further composed

of 3 sectoral representatives. It is noted that under said provision, the sectors for women and workers are already assured of one seat each. With respect to the other sectors, such as the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons or any other sector, the Sanggunian shall determine within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the next local elections which sector from among the other sectors shall be represented in their respective Sanggunians. Section 41 (b) Of the Local Government Code of 1991 has to be reconciled with Section 457 of the same Code with respect to the composition of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. As to the latter, again, it is provided that in addition to the regular and ex- officio members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, there shall be three (3) sectoral representatives in the Sanggunian. What is important to note in Section 457 of the Code is the fact that the women sector is assured of one (1) representation, and that with respect to the workers sector, the Sanggunian is given the option to determine as to whether the sectoral representative for the workers shall come from the agricultural or industrial workers sector. With respect to the third sectoral representative, again, the Sanggunian is given the power to determine from which sector, including the urban poor, indigenous cultura'l communities or disabled persons, shall be represented in the Sanggunian. In this regard, it bears to emphasize further that under the aforesaid Section 457 (c), it is provided that the sectoral representatives Qf(heSungguniang Panlungsed shall be el in th mann r m vi fr I . With the exception of Republic Act No. 8371, otherwise known as the "Indigenous People's Rights Act of IBE" which was said to be already sufficient as an enabling law to install the indigenous peoples representatives in the different Sanggunians of LGUs, Congress has yet to pass a taw providing for the manner of electing the other sectoral representatives in the Sangguniang Panlungsod as mandated under the Local Government Code of 1991. This would answer why at present, with the exception of herein case of Cotabato City, there are still no sectoral representatives in Sanggunians, for that matter, as provided for by the Local Government Code of 1991. We reiterate that Section 457 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 mandates that the sectoral representatives shall be elected in the manner as may be provided for by law. Let it be noted that in the herein case of Cotabato City, Ms. Tabugo was appointed as Women's Sectoral Representative to the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Cotabato Cjry. Well-settled is the rule that appointment is different from election as a manner of acquiring public office. An appointment is the act or designation by the executive officer, board or body to where that power has been delegated, of the individual who is to exercise the functions of a given office (Mechem, Section 102). On the other hand, an election "means the choice or selection of candidates to public office by popular vote through the use of the ballot, and the elected officials are determined through the will of the electorate. An election is the embodiment of the popular will, the expression of the sovereign power of the people. The winner is the candidate who has obtained a majority or plurality of valid votes cast in the election" (Rulloda vs. COMELEC, G.R. No. 154198, January 20, 2003).

Based on the foregoing, it appears that SP Resolution No. 5424 and Executive Order No. 97 are not in order. Pursuant therefore to the power of general supervision of the Department over local government units and their officials, you are hereby directed to advise the Sangguniang Panlungsod and the Mayor of Cotabato City of the foregoing and guide them on the proper course/s of action to take under the circumstances. Thank you. Is/17 Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. P DERO Undersecretary DILG-OUSLG
